title: Past Stories, Food & Second Forms
subtitle: Review past actions through food stories, reading and listening.

units.title: Past Forms in the Kitchen
units.tagline: Use regular and irregular second forms to tell a clear food story.
notes: Use Past Simple for a finished action: Yesterday, I cooked dinner.
Irregular verbs change form: make → made, buy → bought, eat → ate, go → went.
In questions and negatives, use did/didn't + the base verb: Did you make soup? I didn't make soup.

vocabulary.example: Noah followed a simple soup recipe.

vocabulary.meaning: one food item used to make a dish
vocabulary.example: The main ingredient was fresh tomato.

vocabulary.meaning: to move food around with a spoon
to cook food in an oven
vocabulary.example: They baked biscuits for the picnic.

vocabulary.meaning: something you remember from the past
vocabulary.example: The smell created a happy childhood memory.

grammar.title: Past Simple: finished actions
grammar.rule: Geçmişte başlayıp biten eylemler için Past Simple kullanılır. Düzenli fiiller çoğunlukla -ed alır; düzensiz fiillerin ikinci hâli öğrenilmelidir.
examples: Omar made a cake last Sunday.

grammar.title: Questions and negatives
grammar.rule: Did ve didn't geçmiş zamanı zaten taşır; ardından fiilin yalın hâli gelir. 'Did she made?' değil, 'Did she make?' denir.

units.remember: Irregular verbleri üçlü olarak değil, şimdilik fiilin yalın hâli ve ikinci hâliyle birlikte tekrar et: go → went, make → made.
units.watchOut: Did/didn't sonrasında ikinci hâli kullanma: 'didn't went' değil, 'didn't go'.

practice.hint: Make is irregular in the past.
After did, use the base verb.

practice.prompt: The children ___ the soup for ten minutes.
practice.hint: This is a finished action in the past.

practice.prompt: Last weekend, we ___ fresh fruit at the market.
I didn't ___ the recipe before dinner.
practice.hint: The spelling of read stays the same after didn't.

practice.prompt: Which word means one item used to make a dish?
practice.hint: Flour, eggs and milk can all be this.

practice.prompt: Rita ___ the biscuits in the oven.
Choose the best question about yesterday.
practice.hint: Question word + did + subject + base verb.

reading.title: The Unexpected Cookie Recipe
reading.text: Mila wanted to make cookies for her neighbours. She found an old recipe in a book, but the page was difficult to read. First, she mixed butter, sugar and eggs. Then she added small pieces of chocolate because her brother suggested it. The cookies looked unusual, but everyone ate them quickly. Mila wrote the new recipe in her notebook. Years later, she still remembered that afternoon whenever she smelled warm chocolate cookies.

questions.prompt: Why did Mila add chocolate pieces?
What did Mila do after the cookies were eaten?
What helped Mila remember the afternoon later?
Which past verb from the text is irregular?

listening.title: A Cooking Plan
listening.script: Leo: Did you cook last night? Sana: Yes, I made vegetable pasta. I went to the shop after school and bought tomatoes, cheese and oil. Leo: Did you follow a recipe? Sana: No, my aunt showed me how to make it last year. We ate it with bread, and my family said it was delicious.

questions.prompt: When did Sana go to the shop?
Who showed Sana how to make the dish?
Which phrase describes the family's opinion?

units.title: Past Stories & Food Memories
units.tagline: Connect past events in a short, meaningful story.
notes: A past story often answers: when, where, who, what happened and how someone felt.
Use sequence words such as first, then and finally to make a story easy to follow.
Review earlier food language only when it helps the story: menu, dish, dessert and favourite food.

vocabulary.meaning: the time when someone was a child
vocabulary.example: My childhood favourite was rice pudding.

vocabulary.meaning: liked more than all the others
vocabulary.example: Her favourite dessert was apple pie.

vocabulary.meaning: to give part of something to another person
vocabulary.example: The cousins shared the last cookie.

vocabulary.meaning: at the end of a sequence

practice.prompt: First, Nia ___ the vegetables. Then she cooked them.
Which word best completes the sequence: First we ate dinner. ___, we had dessert.
My grandparents ___ me stories about their favourite meals.
Choose the sentence with a correct past form.

options: The time when you were a child
The last part of a recipe

practice.prompt: Last Friday, I ___ my friend at a café.

reading.title: A Dish from Home
reading.text: When Daniel was young, his family visited his grandmother every Saturday. She made a large vegetable dish and put it in the middle of the table. Daniel helped her cut the bread, and his cousins brought the plates. Everyone shared the meal and talked about school. One Saturday, Daniel tried to cook the same dish alone. He forgot one ingredient, but he called his grandmother and asked for help. Finally, the dish tasted different, but it gave him a warm memory of those family meals.

questions.prompt: When did Daniel's family visit his grandmother?
What did Daniel forget when he cooked alone?

writing.title: Write a Food Memory
writing.prompt: Write 6–8 sentences about a food memory. Include when it happened, who was there, what you ate or cooked, and how you felt.
support: Last year / When I was younger, ...
Use at least three Past Simple verbs.

finalQuiz.prompt: Which word can introduce the last step in a story?
